notes: Kinematic swimming reference for the paddle crab, keyframed by eye from blue crab footage (FASTEC clips 000106 and 000094). See kinematic_ref.py for the format and joint conventions.

One paddle stroke is shared by every mode; phase 0 is the paddle upright at the start of its power stroke. Power: broadside (feather 0) sweep up and over the back toward the trailing side. Recovery: feathered edge-on, back to upright and past it toward the leading side.
A paddle that looks broad to a camera faces it, so it is edge-on to a sweep across the image; one that looks thin is broadside to it.

sideways (000106, front view slightly below, the crab swims toward its own left; the robot is mirrored for it, never the footage): the leading paddle strokes up and over the back; the trailing one is held up and out at ~45 deg and strokes out of phase: while the leading paddle recovers (phase ~0.42-0.72) it turns broadside and sweeps out and down to ~20 deg above horizontal, then feathers and rises back. 000106 shows that stroke ~0.15 earlier than 000014; the keys split the difference. The leading hanging leg folds up during the sweep.

paddles_first (000094, side view, anterior on screen left, the crab swims toward its own back, to screen right): both paddles point back and use the same stroke, alternating (the far paddle ~0.6 of a stroke behind the near one); claws held forward, centre legs hanging down and back.
Clips pair up by mode: 000106 (front, slightly below) and 000014 (behind and below) show sideways swimming; 000094 (side) and 000054 (above) show paddles-first swimming.

History: v1 inverted broad/thin; v2 fixed it; v3 matched sweep timing; v4/v5 compared both clips through mirrored footage and misread 000094's orientation; v6 has no mirrored footage, a shared stroke and the paddles_first mode; v7 adds 000014 and 000054 as second views; v8 makes the sideways trailing paddle stroke out of phase (it was keyed hanging and feathering with the leading one) and trims the power-stroke lean to ~50 deg past vertical, as all three clips show.
